title: parseSearch reads a capitalised key's quoted value whole
evidence: packages/domain/src/library.ts:166 TOKEN_RE had no `i` flag while packages/domain/src/library.ts:178 KV_RE reads raw.toLowerCase(); parseSearch('Mood:"dark ambient"') -> tokens [mood:dark], words [ambient]
body:
## Summary
A search key typed with a capital and a quoted value split at the space.

## Description
TOKEN_RE (packages/domain/src/library.ts:166) matched `[a-z_]+:"..."` case-sensitively; KV_RE (library.ts:167) is applied to lowercased text, so `Mood:dark` was a token and `Mood:"dark ambient"` was a one-word token plus a stray free word. Fixed with the `i` flag.

## Flow
- type Mood:"dark ambient" in the Library search
- parseSearch -> {mood: dark} + word ambient
- after: {mood: dark ambient}

## Expected impact
A Library search or agent token with a capitalised key now matches what the lowercase form matches. Nothing else changes: unquoted tokens were already case-blind.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one case rule for quoted and unquoted keys
Before: tokens [mood:dark], words [ambient]; new contract case red (1 failed / 16)
After: tokens [mood:dark ambient], words []; 30/30 green (library.contract, library, library-index)
Method: gate - a new case in packages/domain/test/library.contract.test.ts seeded red on the old regex
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The decision record's bounds are read off SOURCES, not copied
evidence: packages/domain/src/decision.ts: reasons .max(11), note .max(2000) - copies of max(SOURCES[*].maxReasons) and NOTE_LONG in packages/domain/src/source.ts:50,81; no test tied them
body:
## Summary
decisionSchema carried literal copies of the widest source's reason and note bounds.

## Description
packages/domain/src/decision.ts held `.max(11)` and `.max(2000)`, the current widest SourceSpec values (source.ts audio maxReasons 11, NOTE_LONG 2000). A source that grew either would pass checkVerdict and be refused at the record's door. Now REASONS_MAX / NOTE_MAX are derived from SOURCES.

## Flow
- a source raises maxReasons to 12
- checkVerdict admits a 12-reason reject
- decisionSchema refused it (old) / admits it (new)

## Expected impact
No user-visible change today; the next source that widens its vocabulary cannot strand a verdict between the two doors.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source of truth for the verdict bounds
Before: 2 copied literals, 0 tests reading SOURCES against decisionSchema
After: 0 literals; 1 test walking every source's widest verdict through both doors; seeded red twice (max 10, note 500), 18/18 green
Method: gate - new case in packages/domain/test/packet.test.ts + mutant decision-bound-narrower-than-a-source
Result: better
Gate: none

title: kernel decision/apply.ts tests `instanceof AppError` where isAppError is the rule
instrument: a kernel test that throws an AppError from a second module copy (Symbol.for brand, as tests/next-server/exit-store-classify.test.ts does) inside readPacket and asserts claimApply returns {ok:false} instead of rethrowing
evidence: packages/kernel/src/decision/apply.ts:148 `if (!(e instanceof AppError)) throw e;` vs packages/domain/src/errors.ts:99-110 isAppError: 'The only test the codebase uses in place of instanceof AppError' (L44)
body:
## Summary
The apply claim's catch uses instanceof, the check errors.ts says fails across module copies.

## Description
packages/domain/src/errors.ts documents that instanceof AppError fails when a process holds two module graphs (L44) and names isAppError as the only test. packages/kernel/src/decision/apply.ts:148 still uses instanceof, so an AppError from another graph rethrows instead of becoming the apply's 'cannot be read for delivery' outcome. Out of this round's paths (kernel).

## Flow
- readPacket throws an AppError minted by a second copy of @gt/domain
- instanceof is false -> rethrown
- fix: isAppError(e)

## Expected impact
The outbox records a readable 'stuck' line instead of crashing the apply tick. Could break nothing: isAppError is a superset of instanceof.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one AppError test across module copies
Before: 1 instanceof AppError site in packages/kernel/src outside errors.ts
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - the site is in packages/kernel, not this round's paths; the instrument is named
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The style door admits a lock with no approval and pending proofs
instrument: a style.test case refusing a non-grandfathered lock with zero approvals or a pending proof, plus a read of every stored style through the tightened door (kernel styles fixture + an operator-run scan of a store COPY) before landing
evidence: probe: styleSchema.safeParse({status:'locked', lock:{...}, proofs:[], evidence:[]}).success === true; with one pending proof: true. packages/domain/src/style.ts:162-178 superRefine checks status, block, unique ids only; lockBlocker is enforced only by packages/kernel/src/styles/core.ts:117
body:
## Summary
styleSchema accepts a locked style with no approved proof, or with undecided proofs.

## Description
The registry's draft-proofing-locked-ratchet technique (visual-style-locking) makes the lock gate 'at least one approval, zero undecided'. The door (packages/domain/src/style.ts:162) derives status from the lock event alone, and only the kernel's lock op calls lockBlocker; any other writer (v1 import, a seed, the catalogue sync) can store an unratified lock that every consumer then treats as production-ready. Fixed would be a superRefine: a non-grandfathered lock needs >=1 approved proof (and, at lock time, none pending - which the door cannot see, so likely approvals only). Risk 4 because packages/kernel/src/styles/schema.ts:84 reads stored rows through this door with `must`, so one stored violator turns a read into a throw.

## Flow
- a writer stores {lock, proofs: []}
- door admits it, statusOf = locked
- projects build on a style nobody approved

## Expected impact
Projects can only bind styles a human ratified. Could break: reading a stored style that already violates it.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the lock gate held at the door, not only at one writer
Before: door admits 2 of 2 unratified-lock probes
After: 0 of 2 (predicted); stored-row count unknown
Method: probe - the two cases were run against the door; the store side needs a copy only the operator may open
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
drain_note: operator-only: scan a store copy for violators before tightening

title: Packet is z.output where Decision and Style are Parsed
instrument: switch the alias to Parsed<z.output<typeof packetSchema>> and count typecheck errors across the tree (each is a caller reading `x | undefined` where the door guarantees absence)
evidence: packages/domain/src/packet.ts:53 `export type Packet = z.output<typeof packetSchema>;` vs packages/domain/src/decision.ts:57 and style.ts:179 `Parsed<...>`; door.ts:166 Parsed is what parseAt returns
body:
## Summary
The Packet type keeps zod's `?: T | undefined` while parseAt hands out an absent-key shape.

## Description
parseAt returns Parsed<z.output<S>> (packages/domain/src/door.ts:213); Decision and Style alias that shape, Packet aliases raw z.output, so callers holding a Packet see `title?: string | undefined` under exactOptionalPropertyTypes and may write explicit undefined that the door would drop. Changing the alias is a type change with callers outside this scope.

## Flow
- switch the alias
- tsc -b the tree
- fix each caller the stricter type exposes

## Expected impact
Packet joins the door's own optional-key contract. Could break: callers that spread a Packet with explicit undefined.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one optional-key contract for door outputs
Before: 1 of 3 board records not Parsed
After: 0 (predicted); caller fallout uncounted
Method: simulation - caller count needs a tree-wide typecheck on a branch
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: packetIdSchema admits '::', which the decision key's first-split forbids
instrument: operator: `SELECT count(*) FROM packets WHERE id LIKE '%::%'` (and decisions.packet_id) on a copy of foundry-out/gravitone.sqlite; zero rows lets the door refuse '::'
evidence: probe: packetIdSchema.safeParse('a::b').success === true; decisionKey('a::b','c') = 'a::b::c' which every reader splits at the first '::' (packages/kernel/src/decision/schema.ts:234 'packet ids never carry one', lib/decision/v1/types.ts:114, packages/domain/src/decision.ts:21)
body:
## Summary
Three comments state packet ids never carry '::'; no door enforces it.

## Description
decisionKey (packages/domain/src/decision.ts:26) joins `<packet>::<candidate>` and every reader splits at the first '::'. packetIdSchema (ids.ts:36) is any non-empty string, and packetIdOf (lib/ledger/v1/packet.ts:20) keeps the run id verbatim, so a run id holding '::' yields a packet whose decisions re-attach to a different packet id on read. Tightening the door is the fix; it reads stored rows (kernel decision/schema.ts:170,214), so the operator's store must be counted first.

## Flow
- a run id containing '::'
- packet pkt:forge:a::b, key pkt:forge:a::b::cand
- reader splits -> packet pkt:forge:a, candidate b::cand

## Expected impact
A decision can never be filed under the wrong packet. Could break: reading a stored packet that already has '::' in its id.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the key's split rule held at the id door
Before: door admits 'a::b'
After: refuses (predicted)
Method: probe - the door and the join were run; the store count is an operator-only act
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Bound the edit plan's array before zod walks it
evidence: probe: editPlanSchema.safeParse of 65 / 20,000 / 200,000 notes: 1.1 / 9.3 / 21.7 ms (10.7 MB payload)
body:
## Summary
editPlanSchema parses the whole array before checkEditPlan's 64-note bound.

## Description
packages/domain/src/decision.ts editPlanSchema is z.array(...).transform(checkEditPlan); an oversize plan is fully parsed first. Measured cost is negligible, and a zod .max would replace checkEditPlan's counted sentence.

## Flow
- post a 200k-note plan
- parse 21.7 ms, refused

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - refuse an oversize plan earlier
Before: 21.7 ms at 10.7 MB
After: ~0 ms, but the refusal loses its count
Method: probe - timed on three sizes
Result: not-better
Gate: none

title: Compute a style's sheet coverage once per projection
evidence: packages/domain/src/styleView.ts:242-296 calls sheetCoverage directly, via lockBlocker and via styleRefs (3 passes); timed 34.4 us per styleView, 9.5 us per styleSummary on a 30-proof sheet
body:
## Summary
styleView recomputes the block digest and coverage three times.

## Description
Each pass compiles the block and walks the proofs; at 34 us per view a 100-style shelf costs ~3.4 ms. Not worth threading a cached coverage through the ratchet's public functions.

## Flow
- styleView on a 30-proof style, 2000 iterations

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer coverage passes
Before: 34.4 us/view
After: ~12 us/view predicted; 3.4 ms per 100 styles is below any frame budget
Method: probe - timed
Result: not-better
Gate: none
